rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because literal warfare against God is impossible, the phrase means they war against God’s and His Messenger’s allies, or uses a shared figurative sense, avoiding a mix of literal and figurative meanings.
rows.anchor: ومحاربة الله تعالى غير ممكنة، فيحمل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the warfare here as shirk; Abū Ḥayyān says this view is incorrect according to the majority.
rows.anchor: وقول ابن عباس: المحاربة هنا الشرك،

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: ʿUrwa interprets the warfare as apostasy; Abū Ḥayyān says this view is incorrect according to the majority.
rows.anchor: وقول عروة: الارتداد، غير صحيح عند الجمهور،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about warring against God and His Messenger gravely intensifies the seriousness of ḥirāba.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: يحاربون الله ورسوله، تغليظ شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible reading is that their armed violence itself constitutes their corruption in the land.
rows.anchor: والسعي في الأرض فسادا يحتمل أن يكون المعنى بمحاربتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they add corruption in the land to their armed violence.
rows.anchor: أو يضيفون فسادا إلى المحاربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فسادا may be an object of purpose, a verbal noun used circumstantially, or a verbal noun derived from the sense of يسعون, meaning they corrupt the land.
rows.anchor: وانتصب فسادا على أنه مفعول له، أو مصدر في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent rule gives the imam a choice among the four penalties at any rank of ḥirāba; al-Nakhaʿī, al-Ḥasan in one report, Ibn al-Musayyab, Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ, Mālik, and others hold this view.
rows.anchor: والظاهر في قوله: العقوبات الأربع أن الإمام مخير

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik recommends the least severe penalty for a nonkiller, especially one not known for causing harm, but says a killer must be killed.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك: أستحسن أن يأخذ في الذي لم يقتل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو مجلز وقتادة والحسن
rows.claim: A competing view assigns a penalty to each rank: killing brings death, taking property without killing brings cross-amputation, intimidation alone brings banishment, and combining the crimes brings killing and crucifixion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، وأبو مجلز، وقتادة، والحسن أيضا وجماعة:

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومحمد والشافعي
rows.claim: Among proponents of rank-matched penalties, Abū Ḥanīfa, Muḥammad, al-Shāfiʿī, and others, with a report from Mālik, prescribe crucifying the offender alive and stabbing him until death.
rows.anchor: فقال: أبو حنيفة، ومحمد، والشافعي، وجماعة، وروي عن مالك: يصلب حيا

rows.speaker: جماعة
rows.claim: Another group prescribes killing the offender first and then crucifying him as a deterrent; al-Shāfiʿī is also named for this view.
rows.anchor: وقال جماعة: يقتل ثم يصلب نكالا لغيره، وهو قول الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The killing may be carried out by beheading with a sword; another view permits a sword, spear, or dagger.
rows.anchor: والقتل إما ضربا بالسيف للعنق، وقيل: ضربا بالسيف أو طعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The killer need not be legally equivalent to the person killed for this punishment.
rows.anchor: ولا يشترط في قتله مكافأة لمن قتل

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires legal equivalence in applying retaliation for the killing.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: تعتبر فيه المكافأة في القصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported durations of crucifixion include one or three days, until pus flows, or long enough for the crucifixion to be evident.
rows.anchor: ومدة الصلب يوم أو ثلاثة أيام، أو حتى يسيل صديده،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The amputation is of the right hand at the wrist and the left foot at the joint.
rows.anchor: وأما القطع فاليد اليمنى من الرسغ، والرجل الشمال من المفصل

words: ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raised element is not governed like an accusative of accompaniment: that parse would make mere existence accompany its like, whereas the sense is that all earthly things belong to them together with an equal amount.
rows.anchor: فالرافع للفاعل غير الناصب للمفعول معه، إذ لو كان إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parsing ومثله as an accompaniment object governed by the same element as لهم is invalid; Sibawayh calls هذا لك وأباك ugly because no verb or verb-like particle governs it.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه: وأما هذا لك وأباك، فقبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians do allow an adverb or preposition to govern an accompaniment object, which would permit that parse if معه were absent.
rows.anchor: وقد أجاز بعض النحويين أن يعمل في المفعول معه الظرف وحرف الجر

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read ما تقبل in the passive voice.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ما تقبل مبنيا للمفعول.

rows.speaker: يزيد بن قطيب
rows.claim: Yazīd ibn Quṭayb reads the verb actively, meaning that God did not accept it from them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يزيد بن قطيب: ما تقبل مبنيا للفاعل أي: ما تقبل الله منهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted clause is understood: they would offer the wealth and ransom themselves with it; rejection follows from that attempted ransom, not merely from possessing the wealth.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام جملة محذوفة التقدير: وبذلوه وافتدوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat applies to those who meet death still persisting in disbelief, as clarified by 3:91.
rows.anchor: هذا الوعيد هو لمن وافى على الكفر، وتبينه آية آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may coordinate with the predicate of إن, with إن الذين كفروا, or be circumstantial; Abū Ḥayyān considers the circumstantial parse weak.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة يجوز أن تكون عطفا على خبر: إن الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent wording requires amputation for theft as such, whether the stolen item is little or much; the source illustrates this with an egg and a camel.
rows.anchor: والظاهر وجوب القطع بمسمى السرقة، وهو ظاهر النص.

rows.speaker: الحسن والخوارج وداود
rows.claim: A group of Companions and Successors, including al-Ḥasan, along with the Khārijites and Dāwūd, also hold that the wording sets no minimum threshold beyond theft itself.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب جماعة من الصحابة ومن التابعين منهم:

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: Dāwūd and those agreeing with him exclude a single grain or date, setting the threshold at the least thing considered property, even if it is slight.
rows.anchor: وقال داود ومن وافقه: لا يقطع في سرقة حبة واحدة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر وأيمن الحبشي وأبو جعفر وعطاء وإبراهيم والثوري وأبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف وزفر ومحمد
rows.claim: One reported threshold is ten dirhams or more, or the equivalent value in another currency; this is also the position of al-Thawrī and the named Ḥanafī jurists.
rows.anchor: قيل: النصاب الذي تقطع فيه اليد عشرة دراهم فصاعدا،

rows.speaker: عمر وعثمان وعلي وعائشة وعمر بن عبد العزيز والأوزاعي والليث والشافعي وأبو ثور
rows.claim: Another view sets the threshold at a quarter dinar or more, reported from the named early authorities and held by al-Awzāʿī, al-Layth, al-Shāfiʿī, and Abū Thawr.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ربع دينار فصاعدا، وروي عن عمر، وعثمان،

rows.speaker: أنس وعروة وسليمان بن يسار والزهري
rows.claim: Anas, ʿUrwa, Sulaymān ibn Yasār, and al-Zuhrī set the threshold at five dirhams.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خمسة دراهم وهو قول: أنس، وعروة،

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وأبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī and Abū Hurayra are reported to set the threshold at four dirhams.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أربعة دراهم وهو مروي عن أبي سعيد الخدري،

rows.speaker: ابن عمر ومالك وإسحاق وأحمد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, Mālik, Isḥāq, and Aḥmad set the threshold at three dirhams, except that gold requires a quarter dinar.
rows.anchor: ثلاثة دراهم وهو قول: ابن عمر، وبه قال مالك،

rows.speaker: عثمان البتي
rows.claim: ʿUthmān al-Battī sets the threshold at one dirham or more.
rows.anchor: وقيل: درهم فما فوقه، وبه قال عثمان البتي.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr once ordered amputation for theft of one dirham.
rows.anchor: وقطع عبد الله بن الزبير في درهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amputation for theft has additional conditions that are treated in works of fiqh.
rows.anchor: وللسرقة التي تقطع فيها اليد شروط ذكرت في الفقه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read والسارق والسارقة with both nouns in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: والسارق والسارقة بالرفع.

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads the nouns in the masculine plural and follows them with the command to cut their right hands.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: والسارقون والسارقات فاقطعوا أيمانهم،

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Al-Khaffāf reports in Ubayy’s codex السرق والسرقة with a doubled, ḍamma-marked sīn, as recorded by Abū ʿAmr.
rows.anchor: وقال الخفاف: وجدت في مصحف أبي والسرق والسرقة بضم السين المشددة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya suspects that the reported Ubayy form is a copyist’s misreading, since the standard reading without the alif can look the same in writing.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويشبه أن يكون هذا تصحيفا من الضابط، لأن قراءة الجماعة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh parses the nominative nouns as a topic with an omitted predicate, understood as their ruling among what is recited or prescribed.
rows.anchor: والرفع في والسارق والسارقة على الابتداء، والخبر محذوف

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh rejects the imperative as the direct predicate because the fāʾ does not enter the predicate of a topic introduced by al plus a participle in this construction.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز سيبويه أن يكون الخبر قوله:

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر وابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read والسارق والسارقة in the accusative as an instance of الاشتغال.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر وابن أبي عبلة: والسارق والسارقة بالنصب على الاشتغال.

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says accusative is the usual Arabic form, like زيدا فاضربه, but explains the majority’s nominative reading with an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه: الوجه في كلام العرب النصب كما تقول: زيدا فاضربه، ولكن أبت العامة إلا الرفع

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh’s nominative analysis supplies an omitted predicate; he does not make the imperative the predicate, which would violate his rule about fāʾ after this kind of topic.
rows.anchor: تأوله على إضمار الخبر فيصير تأوله: فيما فرض عليكم حكم السارق والسارقة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says al-Rāzī falsely accuses Sibawayh of attacking the widely transmitted nominative reading; Sibawayh actually provides a grammatical parse for it.
rows.anchor: هذا تقول على سيبويه، وقلة فهم عنه، ولم يطعن سيبويه على قراءة الرفع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Sibawayh, the readers’ preference for nominative supports his omitted-predicate parse: with the fāʾ present, the imperative cannot serve as a direct predicate, weakening accusative by الاشتغال.
rows.anchor: فقوله: أبت العامة إلا الرفع تقوية لتخريجه، وتوهين للنصب على الاشتغال

rows.speaker: جماعة من البصريين
rows.claim: Some Basran grammarians allow the nouns as a topic with the imperative as predicate, treating al plus its participle as a generic relative meaning whoever steals.
rows.anchor: وقد أجاز ذلك جماعة من البصريين أعني: أن يكون والسارق والسارقة مبتدأ،

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh allows a raised noun before an imperative when it is an independent topic with an omitted predicate or follows a suppressed demonstrative, as in الهلال والله فانظر إليه.
rows.anchor: فكيف يكون طاعنا في الرفع، وهو يقول: أنه يحسن ويستقيم؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verse by an unnamed poet illustrates an imperative following a noun whose relation is already supplied by an implicit pronoun, supporting Sibawayh’s two-clause analysis.
rows.anchor: وأكرومة الحيين خلو كما هيا

rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī claims Sibawayh preferred the accusative over the nominative reading transmitted from the Prophet and early community; Abū Ḥayyān says Sibawayh made no such claim and in fact supports nominative.
rows.anchor: قال الفخر الرازي: (فإن قلت) : - يعني سيبويه- لا أقول إن القراءة بالرفع غير جائزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the implication that ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar’s accusative reading lacked transmission: it too is traced to the Prophet and Companions, and its readers and teachers are part of the community.
rows.anchor: بل قراءته مستندة إلى الصحابة وإلى الرسول، فقراءته قراءة الرسول أيضا،

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh records that some people read the nouns in the accusative; he does not say that ʿĪsā invented the reading.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه: وقد قرأ ناس والسارق والسارقة والزانية والزاني،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī’s second objection wrongly assumes Sibawayh ranked accusative as superior in this fāʾ construction; Sibawayh calls it linguistically strong when the fāʾ is absent, while the fāʾ favors nominative here.
rows.anchor: لم يدع سيبويه أن قراءة النصب أولى فيلزمه ما ذكر، وإنما قال سيبويه: وقد قرأ ناس

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh’s examples preferring accusative in commands omit the fāʾ; he separately permits a raised topic followed by an imperative in a two-clause construction.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه: وذلك قولك: زيدا اضربه وعمرا أمر ربه، وخالدا اضرب أباه،

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: A noun cannot be a topic directly predicated by an imperative introduced by fāʾ, as shown by the failure of زيد فمنطلق; Sibawayh therefore disallows that parse here.
rows.anchor: فهذا دليل على أنه لا يجوز أن يكون مبتدأ يعني مخبرا عنه بفعل الأمر المقرون بالفاء

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh permits the accusative through الاشتغال, not by treating the fāʾ as the marker that introduces an imperative predicate.
rows.anchor: أجاز نصبه على الاشتغال، لا على أن الفاء هي الداخلة في خبر المبتدإ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without fāʾ, accusative is preferred after a name, though topic plus imperative predicate is also possible; with fāʾ as predicate marker, that parse is barred unless the topic meets conditions that make it resemble a conditional noun.
rows.anchor: أن الجملة الواقعة أمرا بغير فاء بعد اسم يختار فيه النصب ويجوز فيه الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If fāʾ is coordinate, nominative can be either a topic or a predicate of an omitted topic; accusative is less apt because it requires deleting a clause and its governor and shifting the fāʾ.
rows.anchor: وإن كانت عاطفة كان ذلك الاسم مرفوعا، إما مبتدأ كما تأول سيبويه في قوله: والسارق والسارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān explains Sibawayh’s preference for nominative by its lighter ellipsis: only one part of the topic-predicate relation is omitted, with the fāʾ in its normal place.
rows.anchor: وكان الرفع أولى، لأنه ليس فيه إلا حذف مبتدأ، أو حذف خبر.

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh compares 5:38 with 24:2 and reads the nouns as topics in a prescribed-rulings context, followed later by the imperative rather than built directly on the verb.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الزانية والزاني لما قال تعالى: سورة أنزلناها وفرضناها قال في الفرائض: الزانية والزاني

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh compares the construction to 13:35, where مثل introduces the following description after an understood introductory phrase such as among the stories recited.
rows.anchor: مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون ثم قال بعد فيها: أنهار فيها كذا وكذا

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh supplies an omitted phrase such as among what was prescribed for you is the thief and the female thief, or the thief is among what was prescribed.
rows.anchor: مما فرض عليكم السارق والسارقة، أو السارق والسارقة فيما فرض عليكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says Sibawayh chooses the nominative analysis because it needs only one omitted constituent, unlike the costlier accusative analysis with fāʾ.
rows.anchor: فسيبويه إنما اختار هذا التخريج لأنه أقل كلفة من النصب مع وجود الفاء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ links the punishment clause to the preceding implicit ruling, and the command clarifies that ruling; placing the theft rule after the ḥirāba penalties suits Sibawayh’s contextual ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وجيء بالفاء رابطة الجملة الثانية بالأولى، والثانية جاءت موضحة للحكم المبهم فيما قبل ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī incorrectly treats Sibawayh’s account of the two male offenders as requiring accusative; Sibawayh instead parses that verse using the preceding verse’s wording as context for ellipsis.
rows.anchor: تقدم قبل ذلك ما يدل على المحذوف

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Unlike al plus a participle in 5:38, the dual relative in 4:16 can be a topic with a fāʾ predicate because it meets the conditions for resemblance to a conditional noun.
rows.anchor: ويجوز في: واللذان يأتيانها منكم، أن يرتفع على الابتداء، والجملة التي فيها الفاء خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Rāzī’s proposal that the fāʾ attaches to an implicit theft verb; Sibawayh’s omitted prescribed-ruling phrase already explains the linkage.
rows.anchor: وقد قدره سيبويه: ومما فرض عليكم السارق والسارقة، والمعنى: حكم السارق والسارقة

rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī argues that the nominative, unlike the accusative, makes theft the cause of amputation and that جزاء بما كسبا reinforces this; Abū Ḥayyān replies that both constructions express the same causal relation and either can take that reinforcement.
rows.anchor: قال الفخر الرازي: الرابع: يعني من وجوه فساد قول سيبويه إذا اخترنا القراءة بالنصب، لم تدل

rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says nominative foregrounds the thief, while accusative foregrounds cutting, so nominative must be chosen to condemn theft; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this use of Sibawayh’s priority principle.
rows.anchor: قال الفخر الرازي: الخامس: يعني من وجوه فساد قول سيبويه، أن سيبويه قال: وهم يقدمون الأهم فالأهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh’s rule about stating the more important element first concerns clauses with different actor-object relations; 5:38 has only one relation, predicating the ruling of the thief, so al-Rāzī’s argument does not follow.
rows.anchor: كأنهم يقدمون الذي بيانه لهم أهم، وهم ببيانه أعنى: وإن كانا جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī misapplies Sibawayh’s word-order principle: unlike actor and object, the topic-predicate construction has one relation, namely imposing amputation on the thief.
rows.anchor: والرازي حرف كلام سيبويه وأخذه حيث لا يتصور اختلاف نسبة وهو المبتدأ والخبر، فإنه ليس فيه إلا نسبة واحدة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr criticizes al-Rāzī’s grammar book al-Muḥarrar as departing from grammarians’ terminology and mixing disciplines; Abū Ḥayyān says his own reading confirmed that criticism.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو جعفر يقول: لكل علم حد ينتهى إليه، فإذا رأيت متكلما في فن ما ومزجه بغيره

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers a nominative topic analysis with the imperative as predicate, taking the fāʾ to signal the conditional sense of the relative, whoever steals.
rows.anchor: ووجه آخر وهو أن يرتفعا بالابتداء، والخبر فاقطعوا أيديهما، ودخول الفاء لتضمنها معنى الشرط،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read the nouns in the accusative and that Sibawayh preferred it because an accusative noun before an imperative is better.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر بالنصب، وفضلها سيبويه على قراءة العامة لأجل الأمر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī’s conditional-relative parse for Sibawayh: al plus its participle is fused to its complement and cannot serve as a conditional expression.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه الذي أجازه وإن كان ذهب إليه بعضهم لا يجوز عند سيبويه، لأن الموصول لم يوصل بجملة تصلح لأداة الشرط،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says al-Zamakhsharī misstates Sibawayh: Sibawayh treats accusative and fāʾ constructions separately, permits nominative here only as two clauses with an omitted constituent, and does not prefer ʿĪsā’s reading.
rows.anchor: فليس بصحيح، بل الذي ذكر سيبويه في كتابه أنهما تركيبان: أحدهما زيدا اضربه، والثاني زيد فاضربه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān reiterates that nominative requires only one omitted predicate or topic, whereas accusative requires an omitted clause, another elision, and displacement of the fāʾ; the excerpt ends before completing this sentence.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرنا الترجيح بين رفعه على أنه مبتدأ حذف خبره، أو خبر حذف مبتدؤه، وبين نصبه على الاشتغال بأن الرفع يلزم فيه حذف خبر واحد
